AlexW: quick question — hitting a vector dim mismatch in prod batcher when mixing node + java clients, wondering if anyone seen this exact error?

maria_s: what does the error say exactly?

AlexW: server returns `400 Bad Request: embeddings: dimension mismatch (expected 1536, got 1537)` when the same payload from local curl works. only happens in our batched worker path. :confused:

timothy: are you sure arrays are flattened same order? a stray metadata field could sneak in. also check whether one client encodes ints as strings.

AlexW: payloads are lists of floats. suspecting padding/truncation in the batch helper. Node helper does auto-pad to model.dim, Java helper has a `padTo` arg but default behavior differs.

jen: fwiw the java http client had a bug that appended a trailing `,` in the JSON when list builder was empty for the last item — produced an extra null value length. we fixed that in 0.58.2 but older forks might still have it.

simon: also check for hidden BOM or unicode in the label string that could shift indexing. not common but burned us once.

AlexW: repro snippet from logs:
```
DEBUG embed-batcher: batching 64 -> serialized len checks [1536,1536,1537,1536] -> sending batch -> server error
```

maria_s: can you paste the serialized length code you're using?

AlexW: using node helper `batcher.serialize(embedArray)` from ts-sdk v0.11.10. sample client call: ```js
await client.embeddings.create({
  model: 'redwood-embed-1536',
  input: embeddingsBatch
})
```

timothy: quick checks: 1) ensure no NaNs/Inf (some serializers convert them to `null`) 2) ensure typed array `.length` matches expected 1536 3) if using base64/binary path confirm both clients choose same content-type.

AlexW: step 1 done — no NaNs. step 2 shows the one bad vector has length 1537. stumped where extra value comes from.

jen: can you grep for any `push()` that happens after the vector is constructed? our java builder had an extra `add(null)` in an edge branch.

maria_s: also check backpressure/truncation race if you convert streams -> arrays. streaming code may append an empty buffer slice.

AlexW: good point — the worker uses streaming ingestion then materializes arrays. maybe a leftover empty Uint8Array got decoded into `[0]` at the end.

simon: quick workaround — drop any trailing zeros if you know model dim or explicitly slice to modelDim before sending. eg: `vec = vec.slice(0, modelDim)` — but be careful, if it's a real value you'll lose data.

AlexW: posted small patch request: slice on client side as defensive guard + metric for mismatched-lens. will open PR.

jen: for the auth/retry side — note we also saw a streaming reconnect quirk when token refreshed mid-stream: node SDK would resend with old token and get 401; we added a single-retry on 401 that triggers `auth.refresh()` then replay.

AlexW: any recommended pattern for long-lived workers on Dedicated where tokens rotate?

maria_s: use service key + rotate in k8s secret with rolling restart, or implement short refresh logic: if 401, call refresh and replay once. we added event `auth.on('refresh', ...)` in SDK.

timothy: code snippet for pad guard (JS):
```js
function ensureDim(vec, modelDim){
  if (vec.length > modelDim) return vec.slice(0, modelDim);
  if (vec.length < modelDim) return vec.concat(new Array(modelDim - vec.length).fill(0));
  return vec;
}
```

maria_s: and Java equivalent:```java
float[] ensureDim(float[] v, int modelDim){
  if(v.length == modelDim) return v;
  float[] out = new float[modelDim];
  System.arraycopy(v, 0, out, 0, Math.min(v.length, modelDim));
  return out; // pads with zeros by default
}
```

AlexW: thanks. will add that and the mismatch metric. also will instrument serialization to log original typed array lengths.

deploy-bot: deployed embed-batcher v0.12.3 to staging — includes additional length-checking telemetry. :rocket:

AlexW: awesome — i'll run staging tests and post results. :thumbsup:

simon: if you want, tag me on the PR, i'll review pad/truncate semantics — prefer fail-fast by default (throw) with an opt-in auto-pad flag.

AlexW: will do. final note: discovered another streaming quirk — TS SDK's streaming embeddings endpoint will cut the last chunk if `
` inside metadata string isn't escaped correctly. be careful when streaming CSV-ish strings.

maria_s: noted. let's track two follow-ups: 1) PR for defensive slice/pad + metric 2) audit java forks for trailing comma bug. i'll file tickets.

AlexW: thanks all, closing this thread after PR.```
